parts.problem_md:
A group of students have undertaken a study exploring changes in a river channel every 100 metres.

Identify the type of sampling method used.
parts.solution_md:
**The correct answer is**** A**** **

Systematic sampling is when samples are taken at regular intervals.

The alternative answers are incorrect because:

**B **- Random sampling is when a random number generator is used to select sites

**C **- Stratified sampling is when the sample is representative of the population

**D** - Opportunistic sampling is when the sample is chosen because it is convenient - the most accessible sites for example

parts.problem_md:
A group of students has undertaken an enquiry that investigated changes within a river channel along its course.

Explain **one** factor that affected the students' choice of data collection sites.
parts.solution_md:
They could have chosen sites based on accessibility and safety. **[1]** Each site would need to have a stable, flat bank so students could stand safely near the water's edge, which meant avoiding areas where the bank was steep or heavily eroded. **[1]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> **Mark allocation**
> 
> This answer is assessed using a** point-marked** approach.
> 
> - **One mark** for identifying a valid factor
> - **One mark** for how that factor influenced site selection
> 
> **[2 marks]**
> 
> **Alternative content**
> 
> The answer above is just one example of how to respond to this question. Alternative information that could be provided in the answer includes:
> 
> - Representative: sites are spread across the upper, middle and lower course so that data can be compared across different parts of the river
> - Proximity to school or transport: all sites need to be reachable within the time available for the fieldwork day
> - Systematic: sites are placed at regular intervals to reduce sampling bias and allow fair comparison
> 
> **Common errors**
> 
> - Describing data collection methods rather than site selection decisions
> - Discussing a risk and how it was managed

> **[exam-tip]**
> The question asks about **site choice,** not what happened on arrival.
> 
> **Think **about how you would choose a particular spot on the river and not somewhere else.
> 
> **Your **second sentence should begin with 'because' or 'so that' to earn the development mark.

parts.problem_md:
A group of students has undertaken an enquiry that investigated changes within a river channel along its course.

Identify **one **health and safety risk that the students could face during their enquiry. Explain the impact this risk could have had.
parts.solution_md:
One risk is that the riverbank could be wet and slippery after rainfall. **[1]** This could cause a student to lose their footing and fall into the river, resulting in injury or being swept downstream. **[1]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> The command words '**identify**' and '**explain**' together mean you must name the risk and then state what harm it could cause. Do not describe how the risk was managed.
> 
> **Mark allocation**
> 
> This answer is assessed using a** point-marked** approach.
> 
> - **One mark** for identifying a relevant health and safety risk
> - **One mark** for explaining the impact of that risk, not the management of it
> 
> **[2 marks]**
> 
> **Alternative content**
> 
> The answer above is just one example of how to respond to this question. Alternative information that could be provided in the answer includes:
> 
> - Fast-flowing or deep water: a student who entered the water could be swept away
> - Uneven or submerged rocks: a student wading in the river could cut their feet or trip and fall
> - Overhanging or unstable vegetation: a falling branch could strike and injure a student working below
> - Any other appropriate response
> 
> **Common errors**
> 
> - Describing data collection methods rather than site selection decisions
> - Discussing a risk and how it was managed

> **[exam-tip]**
> **There **is an important difference between a risk and a risk management strategy.
> 
> - The risk is what could go wrong.
> - The management is how you tried to stop it.
> 
> **This** question only wants the risk and its impact. Describe the worst realistic outcome, and you will get both marks.

parts.problem_md:
Outline each of the **three** following sampling methods used in geographical investigations.

- random sampling
- stratified sampling
- systematic sampling
parts.solution_md:
Accept for up to max marks answers defining each of the three methods.

Systematic sampling = sample taken in regular way **(1) **e.g. every tenth person; every 100 metres **(1)**...

Random sampling = sample taken based on equal chance of inclusion for all **(1) **e.g. using random numbers table; drawn from a hat** (1) **….

Stratified sampling = samples are selected according to a known characteristic** (1)** e.g. age-distribution of population in an opinions survey; sites reflecting rock type in vegetation survey **(1)**….

For responses focussing directly on differences mark on a similar points basis.
